title: Trust Wiring Runbook: Segmentation, RBACv2, and SIEM Evidence Automation
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures a pragmatic, auditable approach for wiring trust inside Private deployments (VPCs) — focusing on segmentation patterns, RBAC v2 enforcement points, standardized audit log schema, SIEM export shape, and an evidence automation pipeline for compliance artifacts.

Audience:
- Platform engineers implementing Private deployments
- SRE/security engineers responsible for evidence collection and SIEM integration
- Solutions engineers verifying customer-hardened topologies

Scope / Non-scope:
- In-scope: VPC segmentation patterns, firewall/SG baseline rules, mTLS provisioning for inter-service traffic, RBAC v2 mapping to network/agent controls, audit log format and automated evidence packaging for SOC requests.
- Out-of-scope: IAM identity provider onboarding (IdP-specific SSO flows), host-level OS hardening (separate checklist).

Assumptions (quick):
- Customers deploy Redwood Private with private control plane or bring-your-own-control-plane (BYO).
- All service-to-service auth must be mTLS; no plaintext internal HTTP allowed except local dev variants.
- Logs are shipped to customer SIEM via a configurable forwarder or Syslog/HTTP collector that supports TLS and structured JSON.

High-level network pattern (textual diagram):
- Public Boundary: Bastion / VPN / ALB (ingress) -> Customer-managed perimeter
- Management Network (isolated): control-plane agents, metrics exporters, vault proxies
- Workload Network (segmented): inference-pools, shared-caches, monitoring endpoints
- Evidence Export Path: log-forwarder -> local log-aggregator -> secured SIEM egress cluster
(Notes: Each arrow above represents enforced firewall policy + mTLS identity check.)

Baseline VPC segmentation recommendations (practical):
- Create 3 primary subnets per AZ: control-subnet, workload-subnet, infra-subnet.
- Control-subnet hosts management plane endpoints, KMS/NAS proxies; zero inbound from workload-subnet except via defined service proxies.
- Workload-subnet contains model-serving nodes; access limited to known ports and to the egress proxies only.
- Infra-subnet hosts logging/forwarder endpoints + observability agents; log-forwarder has an explicit allowlist for SIEM collectors.

Firewall / Security Group baseline (start-given rules):
- Deny-by-default; explicit allowlist only.
- Control plane inbound: TCP 22/443 from admin CIDR(s) + VPN; mTLS required on 443 for API endpoints.
- Agent heartbeats: UDP/TCP ephemeral to control plane over authenticated channel (mTLS).
- Model inference ports: TCP 8080 (intra-cluster) only allowed from API gateway and autoscaler IPs; block world.
- Egress: allow outbound to SIEM endpoints on TCP 443 and Syslog TCP 6514; all egress flows must be labeled for audit.

RBAC v2: mapping + enforcement points (practical checklist):
- Principle: push policy evaluation to the boundary where identity is strongest. For Private deployments we recommend a split model:
  - Control-plane RBAC (central): token issuance, provisioning, and high-level role mapping (owner, operator, observer).
  - Node/Agent enforcement (local RBAC adapters): mTLS certificate metadata mapped to runtime roles (eg: model-servicing, log-forwarder, admin-agent).

- RBAC v2 artifacts to produce per deployment:
  - role_manifest.yaml (human-readable mapping: role -> allowed actions -> network scopes).
  - enforcement_points.md (lists where to enforce: control-plane API, agent-gateway, gateway firewall, service-proxy).

- Example mapping (text):
  - role: deployer -> can: create/deploy model endpoint; network-scope: can call control-plane API from admin CIDR; cannot access KMS.
  - role: observability -> can: read metrics/logs; network-scope: infra-subnet only, read-only SIEM egress token.

Audit log schema (canonical JSON fields and examples):
- Rationale: SIEMs expect consistent structured events. Schema below is a minimal superset for evidence intake and automated reconciliation.
- Canonical fields (flat key names): timestamp, event_id, source_service, source_host, deployment_id, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, network_src_ip, network_dst_ip, tls_peer_identity, auth_method, outcome, request_id, trace_id, raw_payload

- Example event (as plain text JSON):
  {
    "timestamp": "2026-02-27T19:03:22Z",
    "event_id": "evt-7f3b2a1",
    "source_service": "control-plane-api",
    "source_host": "cp-01.use1.internal",
    "deployment_id": "dep-12345",
    "tenant_id": "team-acme",
    "actor_id": "svc-deployer",
    "actor_role": "deployer",
    "action": "create:model-endpoint",
    "resource_type": "endpoint",
    "resource_id": "ep-78",
    "network_src_ip": "10.2.3.12",
    "network_dst_ip": "10.2.1.4",
    "tls_peer_identity": "CN=agent-1,OU=redwood,deployment=dep-12345",
    "auth_method": "mTLS",
    "outcome": "success",
    "request_id": "req-88aa",
    "trace_id": "trace-ff12",
    "raw_payload": "{...}"
  }

- Special notes:
  - All security-relevant events must include tls_peer_identity when applicable. Siem mappings should index actor_role and tenant_id for rapid queries.
  - request_id and trace_id must be propagated across proxies to link logs to traces.

Evidence automation pipeline (recommendation):
1) Local agent aggregates: rotation window (daily) produces compressed bundles of all control-plane logs, firewall-change events, and RBAC policy diffs for the last 24h.
2) Sign & stamp: each bundle signed using a rotation key (KMS/HSM) and includes a manifest.json (fields: bundle_id, start_ts, end_ts, signer_cert, sha256).
3) Forwarder pushes to customer SIEM or to a secure object-store (S3-like) with strict ACLs. If to object store, forwarder emits a SIEM event linking to object URL + signed manifest.
4) Retention and retrieval: maintain index in control-plane DB for 1 year + archived bundles longer if requested by customer.

Automation example: minimal manifest fields (text):
  bundle_id: bndl-20260227-01
  start_ts: 2026-02-27T00:00:00Z
  end_ts: 2026-02-27T23:59:59Z
  files: [control-audit.log, firewall-changes.json, rbac-diff.json]
  signer_cert: -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...
  sha256: 1a2b3c...

SIEM export format and recommended parsers:
- Preferred transport: HTTPS with mTLS mutual auth to SIEM collector (Syslog over TLS allowed but JSON-over-HTTPS preferred).
- Content type: application/json with envelope: {"events": [ ...canonical events... ], "bundle_id": "..." }
- Parsers to provide to customers: mapping tables for event->Splunk sourcetypes, ELK ingest pipelines with GROK+json, and QRadar DSM example fields.

Search recipes (quick):
- Suspicious RBAC changes (last 24h): actor_role: "deployer" AND action: "update:rbac" AND outcome: "success"
- Unexpected mTLS peer (new CN): tls_peer_identity NOT IN known_cert_store AND outcome: "failure"
- Firewall rule drift: resource_type: "firewall-rule" AND action: "delete"

mTLS provisioning & rotation (practical runbook):
- Certificate hierarchy: Root CA (customer-managed or Redwood-managed per contract) -> Intermediate CA for deployment -> leaf certs per service (CN includes service and deployment id).
- Provisioning steps:
  1) Create CSR with service metadata.
  2) Submit CSR to CA via authenticated API.
  3) Install cert + chain into agent with immutable path and restart agent.
  4) Verify connectivity to control-plane and signature verification.
- Rotation policy: leaf certs rotate every 30 days by default; intermediates annually. Rotation automation must: pre-provision new cert, warm connection, then swap and revoke old cert after grace period.
- Emergency rotation: documented playbook with immediate revocation and forced re-issue; triggers: private key compromise, lateral movement detection.

Hardening checklist (operational, checklist style):
- Infrastructure setup:
  [ ] Deny-by-default VPC firewall applied
  [ ] Control-plane endpoints restricted to admin CIDRs + mTLS only
  [ ] SIEM forwarder endpoint exists in infra-subnet with ACLs

- RBAC and policies:
  [ ] role_manifest.yaml present in repository with change history in Git
  [ ] Automated policy diffs shipped to audit bundle daily
  [ ] Enforcement adapters deployed to agents and gateways

- Logging & evidence:
  [ ] All control-plane APIs emit canonical audit events
  [ ] Request/trace IDs propagate across proxies
  [ ] Bundles are signed and stored to configured object store
  [ ] SIEM mapping configured and smoke tested (example queries return expected rows)

- mTLS & certs:
  [ ] CA chain provisioned and documented
  [ ] Rotation automation enabled; test rotation executed in staging
  [ ] Revocation flow tested (CRL/OCSP or internal revocation index)

- Emergency readiness:
  [ ] Runbook for immediate evidence freeze and bundle export
  [ ] Incident playbook: revoke, rotate, re-key and notify customers

Diagram notes (placeholders for actual diagrams):
- Include: VPC subnet layout, control-plane -> agent mTLS handshake flow, SIEM ingestion pipeline, and evidence pipeline with signing.
- Diagram file names (to attach when finalizing): trust-wiring-vpc-diagram.svg, evidence-pipeline-sequence.png

Operational caveats and tradeoffs (short):
- Strict deny-by-default reduces blast radius but makes debugging harder; ensure temporary allowlist workflows exist with TTL.
- Aggressive cert rotation increases operational overhead for customers without automation; default should be conservative unless customer opts in.
- Bundling frequency: hourly bundles increase fidelity but raise storage/ingest costs. Default daily bundles + on-demand freeze-forensic export recommended.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Formalize RBAC role vocabulary across product teams (action taxonomy). Owner: Marco. JIRA: JIRA-PD-4821.
- Q2: Decide default signer model (Redwood-managed KMS vs customer-managed). Security to propose options.
- Q3: Define acceptable SLAs for evidence packaging and retrieval (target: 1 business day).

Next actions (short-term):
- PR: add role_manifest.yaml template to infra repo (owner: Daniel). (github: GITHUB-PR-7892)
- Spike: implement daily bundle signer prototype in staging (owner: Priya)
- Validation: run SIEM ingest smoke test for sample deployment (owner: Aisha)

Notes to reviewers: prioritize parsability (flat keys), minimal required fields for evidence, and clear mapping from RBAC events to network artifacts. This doc is a working runbook — expect iteration after the first customer pilot.

References / links:
- Confluence: /display/SEC/Private+Deploy+Audit+Templates (CONFLUENCE-PII-ARCH-2374)
- Jira: PD-4821 ticket for RBAC taxonomy alignment
- Slack thread: #private-deploy-security (pinned examples)

End of runbook (working draft).
